speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; to help me identify the cause, please describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse. Also, did this injury happen suddenly after an event, or has it developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis (with a differential consideration for a Charcot joint given the remote trauma and family history of inflammatory arthritis).

I need to confirm if you have tenderness specifically over the thumb base when I press there, and whether you feel a clicking sensation in your wrist during movement. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of the right wrist.
